sources.supports: InnoDB uses server master key and tablespace keys; keyring must remain available; loss of master key is unrecoverable. Client need not receive encryption keys.

COUNT(*) counts transaction-visible rows including NULL; normally traverses smallest secondary index, clustered if none. This definition needs neither payload interpretation nor decryption expression.
InnoDB approximate row estimate, documented deviations40–50%, not bounded few-percent guarantee.

conclusions.case: Application/column encrypted payload; DB stores one ciphertext row per record
conclusions.answer: COUNT(*) requires SQL SELECT access, not application encryption key or plaintext; this follows from documented row-count semantics. Do not use COUNT(AES_DECRYPT(...)), which is unnecessary and counts non-NULL expression results instead of all rows.
conclusions.evidenceType: inference from official COUNT semantics; actual least-privilege test pending

conclusions.answer: SQL counting client does not need master/tablespace key; engine uses server keys. Index scan still causes I/O/CPU/cache/MVCC costs; no zero-impact guarantee.
conclusions.evidenceType: official TDE architecture plus COUNT semantics; existing91 TDE tests use SQL without passing encryption key

conclusions.case: TDE key missing from MySQL server
conclusions.answer: Not equivalent to client lacking key. Do not promise current exact COUNT or sampling access. Retained metadata may be stale and cannot prove current count. Recovery/key restoration belongs to operator.
Outside supported SQL path; no exact or few-percent current count established from ciphertext bytes/file size alone.

Integer-cell estimator queries index ranges and counts rows; no plaintext payload or crypto key is input. It requires accessible single integer unique primary key, stable read snapshot, validated confidence/stop rules and enough budget. An encrypted/UUID/binary/composite key is not applicable to this implementation. Existing known-count or fixed-seed fixture is an evaluation oracle/reproducibility tool, not a production input.
conclusions.evidenceType: inspected bench/samplinglib.py and docs/probability-count.md; no new runtime assertion
